text.p: Southcorp Holdings Ltd's managing director Graham Kraehe said on Wednesday he would consider possible alliances for its appliance division.

"It means a liason or an alliance. It could be from a whole load of options from joint ventures to equity partnerships to just simple alliances such as an R&D (research and development) alliance," Kraehe told reporters after a delivering a speech to a Securities Institue of Australia luncheon.
Southcorp's appliance unit reported a five percent rise in sales to A$985 million for the year to June 30, 1996, but profit before tax and interest fell 27.8 percent to A$37 million.
Kraehe said the alliance could involve local players in the appliance market. Southcorp's competitors in the the market include Email Ltd and Fisher & Paykel Industries Ltd .
He also reiterated that Southcorp was comfortable of achieving analysts' earnings forecasts for the 1996/97 year.

"The market has generally got us rising in the mid-teens, which moves us from A$118 million in 1996 to somewhere in the mid-130's (million), we were comfortable with that and we remain comfortable with that," Kraehe said. Last week, Kraehe told Reuters in an interview that he expected to meet the forecasts.
The diversified Southcorp is also a winemaking and packaging group.
At 3.15 p.m. (0415 GMT), Southcorp shares were four cents up at A$3.73.
